title: The verifier's spoiled-ballot openings: definitions, clocks, boards and pinned panels, with the row 6.2 and the report's openings
generator: packages/crypto/scripts/verifier-openings-vectors.py, from verifier-ballots-vectors.py, verifier-ceremony-vectors.py and challenge-vectors.py (independent Python implementations); the ballot records are verifier-ballots.json's

cases.description: Close falls in period 2, so s_S is at least 3. A ballot in segment 0 (counted whatever s_S is) and one in segment 4 (counted only if s_S ≥ 4); an honest opening in segment 3 (early); in segment 5 an opening of every check failure, one that doesn't decode, an honest one, one of a vote outside the rules, and two that re-use one ballot's (v_j, r_j) under other share hashes: the segment-0 ballot's (cast) and the segment-4 ballot's (undecided); in segment 6 a byte-identical copy of the honest one and of the stray one, and in segment 7 a third copy of the honest one (repeats, each of the first). The honest openings above the floor may still be early or late once s_S is known, so 6.2 is unverifiable.

Every opening breaks a rule the floor decides: an honest one in segment 3 (early), one re-using the segment-0 ballot's commitment (cast), one failing opening-vss, and a copy of the cast one (repeat). 6.2 fails at the first, opening-early.
The first settled opening doesn't decode (a trailing byte), and a stray one follows in a later segment: 6.2 fails with decode and its decoding code.
Only honest openings above the floor, opening no ballot on the copy: undecided until s_S is known, so 6.2 is unverifiable.
An opening that re-uses the commitment of a ballot in segment 4, above the floor: whether that ballot is counted needs s_S, so no break is reported and 6.2 is unverifiable.

An opening that re-uses the commitment of a ballot in segment 3, the floor itself (client rule 1 lets a ballot cast in close's period carry it): counted whatever s_S is, so the opening is cast and 6.2 fails.
The same board as settled under a clock whose epoch is after close: the floor is below 0, so nothing is early or counted by it, and only the repeat and the failing check settle their openings.

The profile pins spoiled-ballot opening version 2 beside ballot version 1, whose cores only opening version 1 opens: 2.3 fails, and 6.2 is not reached, since no opening is judged against an election it can't open the ballots of.
